title: Spider-Man

sources.label: PinkNews — theatrical and ITV2 dialogue comparison

synopsis: Peter Parker discovers his powers as a teenager. After Uncle Ben dies, he must decide what he owes the strangers he can now protect.
verdictRationale: Ben’s rebuke after Peter strikes Flash gives him a measure for every later fight. At the bridge, the Goblin tries to make Peter choose whose life is worth saving. Peter tries to save everyone.
ageRationale: The final beating and impalement are intense, and May is attacked in her bedroom. The rain-soaked kiss and a wrestling insult also merit discussion.
reflection: Peter sits at May’s hospital bedside after going after the man he blames for Ben’s death. A family mourning someone may recognize both impulses. Sitting beside the person who is still here is a work of mercy Peter can actually offer.

themes.evidence: Peter taunts the male wrestler by suggesting a husband gave him his outfit. This is an insult, not an identified couple. ITV2 shortened the line in a later broadcast.

title: Spider-Man 2
synopsis: Peter’s efforts to hold a job, love Mary Jane and serve the city begin to collide as Otto Octavius loses control of a fusion experiment.
verdictRationale: Peter saves children at the cost of his delivery job and tells May a truth he knows will hurt. The train passengers later take a risk for him. Heroism here includes accepting help and admitting fault.
ageRationale: The attack on hospital staff has the pacing and imagery of a horror scene. A runaway elevated train and the kidnapping of May sustain the peril.
reflection: Peter has spent much of his life hiding his face. On the train, people see how young and exhausted he is and carry him. Receiving care can require as much humility as offering it.

title: Spider-Man 3
synopsis: Public acclaim and a powerful alien suit feed Peter’s pride as Harry seeks revenge and Peter learns more about Ben’s death.
verdictRationale: Peter’s revenge harms Mary Jane and leaves Harry scarred. His eventual mercy toward Flint Marko and Harry’s decision to protect Peter give the story moral weight. The film lets the audience see who pays for Peter’s pride.
ageRationale: Peter strikes Mary Jane during a club fight. A blade impales a character, an explosion disfigures Harry, and Venom threatens a captive.
reflection: Eddie takes his anger into church and asks for a man’s death. Peter also wants an enemy punished. Orthodox prayer for enemies asks for a harder change in the person praying, a change visible when Peter hears Marko out.
